items.title: The classifying stack of a finite group
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a finite abelian group (for instance $G=\mathbb Z/2$), viewed as the constant group scheme $G_k$ over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]), acting trivially on $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $BG$ be the category fibred in groupoids over $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]], [[def-fppf-topology-on-schemes]]) whose fibre category over a $k$-scheme $T$ has as objects the right $G$-torsors over $T$ - fppf coverings $P\to T$ with a right $G$-action such that $G_k\times_kP\to P\times_TP$, $(g,p)\mapsto(pg,p)$, is an isomorphism - and as morphisms the isomorphisms of torsors. Then $BG$ is a stack in groupoids over $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]) and an algebraic stack over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-stack-and-inertia]]) with presentation $\operatorname{Spec}k\to BG$ given by the trivial torsor $G_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. For every torsor $P$ over $T$ the automorphism sheaf of $P$ as a right $G$-torsor is canonically $G_k$ (left multiplication), so for abelian $G$ the inertia stack satisfies $\mathcal I_{BG}\cong G_k\times_kBG$; over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ its objects are the pairs (trivial torsor, $g$) with $g\in G$.
items.strategy: Verification. (1) Pullbacks of torsors along morphisms of $k$-schemes exist and are unique up to canonical isomorphism, so $BG$ is fibred in groupoids. (2) Descent: an fppf descent datum for torsors $P_i/T_i$ consists of cocycle-compatible isomorphisms; each $P_i\to T_i$ is affine because it becomes the projection $G_k\times_kP_i\to P_i$ after the fppf base change $P_i\to T_i$, and affineness descends by [[lem-nonaffine-affine-and-finite-morphism-fppf-descent]]; the datum therefore glues to an affine scheme $P\to T$ by the published effective faithfully flat descent of affine algebras ([[lem-faithfully-flat-effective-descent-of-modules-and-algebras]]) after replacing the family by the single fppf cover $\coprod_iT_i\to T$; the $G$-action and the trivialization isomorphism are compatible with the descent datum and descend as morphisms by [[lem-nonaffine-fppf-descent-of-scheme-morphisms]]. Hence $BG$ is a stack in groupoids. (3) The trivial torsor gives a 1-morphism $x\colon\operatorname{Spec}k\to BG$; for any $T\to BG$ corresponding to a torsor $P$, the 2-fibre product $\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{BG}T$ is $P$, a scheme, so the diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces. The projection $P\to T$ is smooth: after the fppf base change $P\to T$ of the source it becomes the projection $G_k\times_kP\to P$, a base change of the finite etale (hence smooth) morphism $G_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and smoothness is local on the source; it is surjective because it is a covering. Thus $BG$ is an algebraic stack. (4) An automorphism of a right $G$-torsor $P$ over $T$ is left multiplication by a unique element of $G(T)$, so the inertia fibre category over $T$ consists of pairs $(P,g)$ with $g\in G(T)$; for abelian $G$ two such objects are isomorphic exactly when they have the same $g$, giving the fibre category of $G_k\times_kBG$. The nonabelian case gives the conjugation quotient groupoid $[G/G]$ and is not needed here.

items.title: A quotient stack need not be a scheme
items.statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $G$ be a nontrivial finite group, viewed as the constant group scheme over $k$ ([[def-group-scheme-over-a-field]]); for instance $G=\mathbb Z/2$. The classifying stack $BG$ of [[ex-classifying-stack-of-a-finite-group]] is an algebraic stack over $k$ ([[def-algebraic-stack-and-inertia]]) but is not equivalent to the stack $\mathcal S_X$ of any $k$-scheme $X$ ([[def-scheme]], [[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]). In particular, the quotient stack of the trivial action of $G$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is not a scheme, although the corresponding fppf quotient sheaf ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]]) is the representable sheaf $h_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$: the passage from quotient sheaves to quotient stacks genuinely enlarges the category.
items.strategy: Proof. For a $k$-scheme $X$, the fibre category of $\mathcal S_X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is the discrete groupoid on the set $X(k)=\operatorname{Mor}_k(\operatorname{Spec}k,X)$ ([[def-descent-data-and-stack-in-groupoids]]); in particular all its automorphism groups are trivial, and by [[lem-inertia-of-a-stack-in-setoids]] its inertia is itself. An equivalence of stacks in groupoids induces equivalences of fibre categories ([[def-category-fibred-in-groupoids]]), and a groupoid equivalent to a discrete groupoid has trivial automorphism groups. But the fibre category $BG(\operatorname{Spec}k)$ contains the trivial torsor $G_k$, whose automorphism group is $G_k(k)\cong G$ by the automorphism computation of [[ex-classifying-stack-of-a-finite-group]]; this group is nontrivial, a contradiction. Finally, for the trivial action the naive quotient presheaf of the pre-relation $G\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k\rightrightarrows\operatorname{Spec}k$ is already $h_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$, so its fppf quotient sheaf is $h_{\operatorname{Spec}k}$ ([[def-quotient-sheaf-and-representable-quotient]] is the field-level convention used for this comparison); the quotient stack is $BG$, which is not even a scheme. The example separates quotient sheaves, algebraic spaces and stacks.
